AI engineer hiring (Swiss agentic/RAG/governance roles, Stanford HAI 23% positive)

AI coding agents (three of HN's top four are critiques of the practice, not the tools — 'don't be a meat proxy' at 1,804 points on humans relaying unread model output, 'LLMs reward expertise' at 1,354 on leverage scaling with existing skill, and a proposal to retype generated code by hand as forced comprehension; the sharpest line is that the prompt/paste-error/retry loop has been rebranded 'agentic engineering')

Implementation & services revenue (the labour side of the trade shows up in the Swiss job file — the forward-deployed-engineer title has spanned Team Lead to zero-years-required inside one country in one week, and the newest posting names no LLM, RAG, prompt or agent requirement at all, listing Claude and Gemini in the benefits stack beside Kubernetes and Postgres)

AI coding agents (Meta enters the coding-agent war with Muse Code - a terminal agent whose differentiator is persistent async background agents that survive the whole session rather than spawning per subtask - and HN finds the story in the pricing: 10x/20x off if you let Meta train on your data, with small print documented as appearing after free credits were already granted at the 1.1 launch; ServiceNow's Build Agent now runs inside every major coding tool governed by default)

Implementation & services revenue (the last-mile thesis gets a matching JD - Orange Business puts 'advising C-level stakeholders on AI strategy, governance, and roadmaps' inside an engineering role, which is the same claim a French practitioner tribune makes from the other side: raw model capability has become a commodity and the contest is decided after the demo; SAP's proof point is a customer cutting HR cycle times 40-60%)

Implementation & deployment revenue (OpenAI opens a second, more senior Zürich deployment seat — Technical Deployment Lead alongside the existing Forward Deployed Engineer — suggesting the function is being built out rather than filled as a one-off; the enterprise-side counterpart is a five-stage agentic adoption maturity model that attributes the deployment gap to operating maturity rather than model quality)
